detail:
MedlinePlus describes Long COVID as a chronic condition that includes a wide range of symptoms or conditions that can range from mild to severe. Many people recover from COVID-19 within days or weeks, but in Long COVID, symptoms last at least three months and may linger for weeks, months, or years, sometimes resolving and later returning.

Reported symptoms span body systems: fatigue and fever; cough and trouble breathing; chest pain and palpitations; brain fog, headache, sleep problems, dizziness, and tingling; and digestive symptoms such as diarrhea, constipation, and stomach pain. Most people's symptoms slowly improve over time, but for some they persist much longer, and evaluation focuses on documenting the pattern and excluding other causes.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about symptoms that persist after COVID-19.
summary: MedlinePlus describes Long COVID as a chronic condition that can follow SARS-CoV-2 infection, in which symptoms last at least three months and can affect many body systems, from fatigue and brain fog to breathlessness and palpitations.
takeaways: symptoms can linger, disappear, and return
there is no single test that diagnoses long covid
post-exertional malaise is a recognized feature
new or worsening symptoms after covid deserve a doctor's review
title: Long COVID: symptoms that persist for months
